name: patch_tick
description: Cheat-Engine-style value freeze: the attacker repeatedly writes the same bytes to the same target address at a fixed interval, mimicking the trainer pattern where the 'Active' checkbox next to a value in the CE address list keeps that value pinned even as the game tries to update it. Uses the existing patch-memory verb with --tick-count 20 --tick-interval-ms 50 so a full freeze burst takes about 1 second and produces exactly 20 WRITEVM_REMOTE events to the same base_address. Distinct temporal signature vs patch_direct (single write): write_span_seconds > 0, write_rate_hz ≈ 20, cross_process_write_count == 20. Same target address as memorypatch — TestTarget's `value` variable — so the base fingerprint is identical to patch_direct scaled by the tick count.

extra.expected_fingerprint: 20x cross-process WRITEVM_REMOTE events, all with base_address == TestTarget's `value` addr, spaced ~50ms apart → write_span_seconds ≈ 0.95, write_rate_hz ≈ 20. Notably absent: 0x ALLOCVM, 0x PROTECTVM, 0x READVM_REMOTE (verify uses read only at the end), 0x THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE. Discriminator vs patch_direct: write_count = 20 (vs 1); vs patch_aob: no read burst; vs everything else: dominant WRITEVM count with distinct_write_targets == 1 (same address hit repeatedly).
